1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 6 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 84:  p300.aspirate(vol_polymerase, aluminum_block["A2"])
   At line 84 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 6 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   well A2 in slot 2.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [4ac1f072426b]

6. WARNING COLD-MODULE-NEVER-SET: A temperature module was loaded but never set
   line 81:  p300.aspirate(vol_buffer, aluminum_block["A1"])
   At line 81 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, C1, C2, C3 and 9 more in slot
   2, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at
   room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), fwd primer
   (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 2 more sat on a block that was
   never cold; the robot pipetted there 17 times over the run. The person setting up the
   deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, C1, C2, C3
   and 9 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, C1, C2, C3 and 9 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24
   Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 2, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at
   the end.
   Source: Opentrons, temperature module: at room temperature until set_temperature, which
   blocks
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/temperature_module.html
   Source: Thermo Fisher T4 ligase manual: keep on ice, use within minutes
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/t4dnaligase_1U_man.pdf
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   [19285c302e2c]

7. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
   line 85:  p300.dispense(vol_polymerase, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 85 the robot put polymerase into well A1 in slot 3. Take well A1 in slot 3: at
   that moment it held only 120 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at
   line 94, to make the 246 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is
   shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the
   water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat
   buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then
   cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to well A1 in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix
   it, and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [8c4dceb6cdb7]

8. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: fwd primer (well A3 in slot 2)
   line 87:  p300.aspirate(vol_fwd_primer, aluminum_block["A3"])
   At line 87 the tip went into fwd primer (well A3 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer
   (well A1 in slot 2) and polymerase (well A2 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that
   has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock
   now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again,
   so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next
   run.
   Affected: well A3 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 87 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [2e80ff7073ec]

11. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir well A1 in slot 3: 3 × 10 ul in 276 ul
   line 97:  p300.aspirate(10, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 97 the tip mixes well A1 in slot 3 with 3 strokes of 10 ul in a well holding 276
   ul. 3 strokes of 10 ul move 0.11 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of
   strokes to mix (the mixing work). Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three
   mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the
   concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (220.8 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5,
   220.8, well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.

13. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 12 wells of polymerase with a sample
   line 103:  p300.dispense(23, plate[f"A{i}"])
   At line 103 the robot starts putting polymerase into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 1), and 12 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 4 more in slot 1.

findings.title: 6 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 84 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 6 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: well A2 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 81 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, C1, C2, C3 and 9 more in slot 2, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), fwd primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 2 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 17 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, C1, C2, C3 and 9 more in slot 2.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 2, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: polymerase
findings.explanation: At line 85 the robot put polymerase into well A1 in slot 3. Take well A1 in slot 3: at that moment it held only 120 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 94, to make the 246 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to well A1 in slot 3: water and buffer first, then the sample, then polymerase last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: fwd primer (well A3 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 87 the tip went into fwd primer (well A3 in slot 2) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 2) and polymerase (well A2 in slot 2) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 87 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: Mixing too weak to stir well A1 in slot 3: 3 × 10 ul in 276 ul
findings.explanation: At line 97 the tip mixes well A1 in slot 3 with 3 strokes of 10 ul in a well holding 276 ul. 3 strokes of 10 ul move 0.11 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (220.8 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 220.8, well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
